edges.effect_quant: Randomized trials suggest a small average effect that is directionally consistent but not dramatic.
edges.mechanism: DASH lowers sodium density while raising potassium, calcium, magnesium, and plant-food intake, producing measurable effects on vascular tone and blood pressure within weeks. For Cardiovascular disease, its mechanism is strongest where hemodynamics and diet quality are the dominant drivers.
edges.summary: Randomized trials link dash diet pattern to lower risk of cardiovascular disease in general adult. The average effect is usually small rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
